Acute Chronic Workload Ratio

Source: R/ACWR.R
ACWR.Rd

Calculates the acute chronic workload ratio for one or several athletes with one or more methods (see EWMA(), RAC() and RAU()).

Usage

ACWR(
  db,
  ID,
  TL,
  weeks = NULL,
  days = NULL,
  training_dates,
  ACWR_method = c("EWMA", "RAC", "RAU"),
  partial = FALSE
)

Arguments

db

a data frame with one row per session.

ID

name of the column with the ID of the subjects.

TL

name of the column with the training load (numeric, >= 0).

weeks

deprecated and ignored in the calculation. If given, the column is kept in the output.

days

deprecated and ignored in the calculation. If given, the column is kept in the output (e.g. for plot_ACWR()).

training_dates

name of the column with the training dates (Date or POSIXct). Rows do not need to be sorted.

ACWR_method

method(s) to calculate ACWR: any of "EWMA", "RAC" and "RAU".

partial

passed to RAC() and RAU(). If FALSE (default), values are NA until enough history exists; if TRUE, the days available are used.

Value

a data frame with the ID, TL, weeks, days and training dates columns, followed by the acute & chronic training load and ACWR of the selected method/s. Rows are in the same order as in db.

Details

Each athlete's sessions are turned into a daily series from their first to their last date: sessions on the same day are summed and days without a session count as a load of 0.

A missing load (NA) makes every window that contains its day NA, and a single warning is given for the whole data frame.

Package decisions

The following choices are made by this package; they are not taken from the cited sources:

  • RAC and RAU windows move day by day. The sources define acute and chronic loads by weeks (the most recent week, and the average of the last 4 weeks or of the 3 preceding weeks). This package interprets them as rolling windows of 7, 28 and 21 calendar days that end on each day, so every day has its own value.

  • With partial = TRUE, a window that starts before the first day uses only the days available and is rescaled to 7 days (sum x 7 / number of days available). The sources do not cover incomplete windows.

  • For all methods, the ratio is NA when the chronic load is 0 (e.g. no training in the chronic window): a ratio to zero load is undefined, and returning NA avoids infinite values in summaries and plots.

EWMA is updated every calendar day, as defined by Williams et al. (2017); this is not a package interpretation.

Examples

data("training_load", package = "ACWR")

# Calculate ACWR
result_ACWR <- ACWR(db = training_load,
                    ID = "ID",
                    TL = "TL",
                    training_dates = "Training_Date",
                    ACWR_method = c("EWMA", "RAC", "RAU"))

# Athletes with rest days
data("training_load_rest", package = "ACWR")
result_rest <- ACWR(db = training_load_rest,
                    ID = "ID",
                    TL = "TL",
                    training_dates = "Training_Date",
                    ACWR_method = c("EWMA", "RAC", "RAU"))
